A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNoPE-SWA research. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, attention analyses, and training and inference efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results, including model comparisons, NIAH and RULER evaluations, attention distributions, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions remove QK-Norm and combine global NoPE layers with sliding-window RoPE layers. The final architecture retains the 1:3 layer ratio and 4,096-token window; v2's architecture diagram introduces no new component.

E1.justification: Training domains and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including the short-context benchmarks, NIAH, and RULER retrieval and QA. Evaluations through 256k and the longer efficiency probes already appear in v1; Appendix C relocates existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RoPE, QK-Norm, NoPE, the same RNoPE variants, and the final RoPE baseline versus RNoPE-SWA. The newly discussed p-RoPE is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: The stated model sizes, training budgets, learning-rate schedules, context mixtures, evaluation lengths, and metrics remain unchanged. v2 clarifies the hybrid models' training setup but does not document a changed protocol or explain its revised attention values through different settings.

E4.justification: v1 Section 3 reports investigating full-attention layer ordering and finding no effect; v2 removes this brief ablation report. The theta sweep, layer-ratio comparison, and Appendix B attention-distribution and entropy analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 16 random-seed trials per NIAH context-depth combination. Neither introduces additional run-count information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Headline benchmark scores and efficiency measurements remain unchanged, but v2 Figure 1 changes numerous 32k and 128k attention values from v1 Table 3. For example, 128k RoPE needle mass changes from 0.0010 to 0.015, beyond rounding, while v2 Table 8 still reports 0.0010. The PDFs do not explain these discrepancies or establish a rerun.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The attention-mass definition, O(SL) versus O(L²) complexity discussion, and theoretical 75% savings bound remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens short-context performance from being competitive in v1 to surpassing conventional RoPE models in both long- and short-context tasks in v2. Efficiency becomes explicit in the abstract, although it was already a paper-level contribution in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets layer specialization as a spontaneous division of labor emerging without tailored losses or data augmentation, extending v1's description of complementary roles. It also removes the concluding discussion of efficiency and FlashAttention-compatibility challenges for richer contextual-position schemes.

D1.justification: Section 2.2.3 newly states explicitly that hybrid pretraining follows Section 2.1's data and protocol and that theta variants use the same fine-tuning steps and data. This improves documentation without establishing an actual training change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Barbero et al.'s p-RoPE work and expands the comparison with partial-RoPE approaches. Section 3 now distinguishes their within-head modifications from the proposed cross-layer specialization, refining the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites and expands portions of the attention analysis, introduces explicit segment descriptions, renames 'qc' to 'End', and reorganizes related-work paragraphs. It also removes the generic impact statement and shortens the conclusion; the overall section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one and substantially reorganizes its displays. Attention tables become bar charts and a separate score table, an architecture diagram is added, and NIAH summary scores become a table. The 256k heatmaps move to Appendix C, while the separate 128k heatmaps are omitted.

improvement.justification: The architecture diagram, clearer exposition, and p-RoPE discussion improve readability and positioning. However, v2 introduces unexplained contradictions in the attention evidence motivating the architecture: Figure 1 reports 128k RoPE needle mass of 0.015 while Appendix A retains 0.0010, consistent with v1. This weakens quantitative reliability enough to outweigh the presentation gains. The unchanged principal benchmark results limit the overall deterioration.
